subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should `web_fetch` default SSRF policy allow a DNS answer set when at least one resolved address is public, or should mixed blocked/public answers remain fail-closed unless an explicit trusted-network policy opts in?
rationale: The source fix is small, but it changes the default DNS-answer security boundary from any blocked answer fails to only all blocked answers fail.

options.title: Keep strict default
options.body: Leave mixed blocked/public DNS answers blocked by default and steer affected operators to explicit trusted proxy or SSRF policy configuration.

options.title: Filter blocked answers
options.body: Allow requests when at least one resolved address is allowed, but filter blocked records before pinning and add focused regression tests for mixed public/special-use answers and all-blocked answers.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve current default and add a narrow documented config mode for deployments affected by DNS pollution.

recommendation.title: Keep strict default
recommendation.body: Leave mixed blocked/public DNS answers blocked by default and steer affected operators to explicit trusted proxy or SSRF policy configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: History points to `steipete` for the central SSRF host/IP block checks that define this boundary.
